answers.solution:
Diagnosis and fix complete. The self-contained write-up is at `/workspace/scheduler/SOLUTION-SCHED-GAP-1734.md`.

## Root cause

`TestUsagePoolLeaseReleasedWhenStartFails` treated an **empty** `SCHEDULER_DISPATCH_TARGETS` file as "dispatch disabled". It is not: per `dispatch_targets.go`, empty/missing means *"no lane is remote"*, so every lane keeps its historical **local** transport. The test's spawner (`NewSpawner(db, 1)`) had **no gateway client** and `noExecFallback == false`, so `Spawn()` fell through to `exec.Command("hermes", …)` — the live CLI/gateway. The SQLite `RAISE(IGNORE)` trigger makes `StartRunning` return `nil` (only the row update is skipped), so the slot pool proceeds past the cleared gate and dispatches. Confirmed by code trace and a safe repro:

```
SPAWN: start-fails-dbg tick=… pid=… workdir=/tmp
LEAK: hermes invoked with: chat -q [Scheduler tick: start-fails-dbg-…] … Workdir: /tmp.
```

It's intermittent because `SlotPool.Spawn` is fire-and-forget and `Wait` returns when `Running()==0`; when the goroutine loses the race, test cleanup closes the DB first (`sql: database is closed`) and nothing leaks — which is why only some suite runs produced a phantom tick.

## Fix

`internal/scheduler/usage_pool_policy_test.go` — added `newHermeticBookkeepingSpawner` (no gateway client + `SetNoExecFallback(true)`) and used it in the two bookkeeping fixtures, removing the misleading empty-targets setup. `dispatch_targets.go` — documented the "empty ≠ disabled" footgun at `EnvDispatchTargets`. Byte semantics of the targets file are intentionally unchanged.

## Verification

- Fixed test passes, and with a stub `hermes` first on `PATH`, **zero** `hermes` invocations occur; the fixed spawner now logs `DEFERRED … no gateway client and exec fallback disabled`.
- Safe original-vs-fixed A/B demonstrated the leak and its elimination.
- `TestUsagePool*`, `TestRemote*`, `TestDispatchLeg*` pass (`1.045s`), `go build ./...` clean.
- Live-box check documented: count `Scheduler tick: start-fails-` lines in `~/.hermes/foreman/logs/agent.log` before/after — count must not increase while the lease assertion still passes.

Fleet-side detection: fixture-named tick + workdir `/tmp` + empty worker model/provider = leaked test dispatch — report, do not provision.

signatures.description: SYMPTOM: a scheduler unit test mints a REAL foreman tick and dispatches a live Hermes session. Phantom tick ids of the shape <fixture-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-SS> appear in the fleet one per suite run: start-fails-2026-10-05-05-28-58, start-fails-2026-10-07-01-07-44, start-fails-2026-10-07-01-07-50 (double dispatch, 6s apart, consistent with two suite invocations or a -race re-run), start-fails-2026-10-07-17-59-06, start-fails-2026-10-10-10-39-28. Each leaked session consumes one of the scheduler's 10 slots plus a whole foreman turn; the 2026-10-05 instance ran with workdir /tmp, no scheduler project row, an empty worker model/provider, and still went as far as a branch-ref push and a DuckBrain write. ROOT CAUSE: internal/scheduler/usage_pool_policy_test.go, TestUsagePoolLeaseReleasedWhenStartFails, sets SCHEDULER_DISPATCH_TARGETS to a file written with an EMPTY body (writeDispatchTargets(t, "")) believing that neutralizes dispatch. Per internal/scheduler/dispatch_targets.go a missing-or-empty targets file means 'no lane is remote', i.e. every lane keeps its historical LOCAL behavior = spawn through the gateway. The test therefore ENABLES the very dispatch leg it meant to disable. pool.Spawn(PackedProject{Name:"start-fails", Workdir:"/tmp"}) then mints the tick id and drives the spawn to the endpoint leg; resolveTickEndpoint (spawn.go, gateway_endpoint.go) merges the project row's lane/namespace endpoint with the spawner's global gateway, and a project row carrying no gateway_url (the test insert has only name/repo_url/workdir) falls through to the GLOBAL configured endpoint, which is the live gateway. SCOPE DETAIL: sibling fixtures leak nothing - the slot-timeout fixture never clears the slot gate, and the panic fixture uses a nil spawner in a child process - so the offender is specifically the trigger-refused path where the tick clears the slot gate before the queued-to-running status update is ignored. REPRO HAZARD: do NOT reproduce by running go test -run TestUsagePoolLeaseReleasedWhenStartFails on a box with the gateway live; that run itself leaks another tick. VERIFY instead by counting 'Scheduler tick: start-fails-' lines in ~/.hermes/foreman/logs/agent.log before and after the run (the count must NOT increase) while the usage-lease-release assertion still passes. FIX: neutralize the dispatch leg inside the test (point the spawner's gateway endpoint at an unreachable address, or inject a test-double gateway client) instead of relying on an empty dispatch-targets file; optionally add a build-time guard that a test-constructed Spawner never resolves the global endpoint. FLEET-SIDE DETECTION for any future leak: a tick whose id carries a test-fixture name, whose workdir is /tmp, and whose worker model/provider are empty is a leaked test dispatch, not a project - diagnose and report, do NOT provision it.
